inputMapRead.title: Read an input map
inputMapRead.description: Reads a keyboard/gamepad input map by path.

animationGraphRead.title: Read an animation graph
animationGraphRead.description: Reads an animation graph by path.

animationRetargetStatus.title: Read animation retargeting
animationRetargetStatus.description: Reads measured retarget fit for a motion.

commandRunStudioCommand.title: Run a command
commandRunStudioCommand.description: Fires a studio command by its identifier, exactly as a keyboard shortcut or a menu item would. The document it applies to has to be in front. An identifier reads [scope].[verb], and studio.state answers the scope of what is in front: taking an edit of a document back is [scope].undo — scene.undo, canvas.undo, sequence.undo — and putting it back [scope].redo. ONE call takes back ONE gesture, so a second takes back the one before it: read the document again rather than sending it twice. No other action undoes an edit, files.undoFileOperation covering project files alone.

workspaceOpen.title: Open a workspace
workspaceOpen.description: Switches to a workspace, and creates a document there when asked to — a NEW one every time, so it is not the way back to a document already open. A creation wants a title, and the person is the one who gives it: ask them for the name rather than inventing one. A title the project already holds is refused.

modelsSearch.title: Search for a model
modelsSearch.description: Searches generation engines by model name or identifier, family and operation. The query is optional and names the engine, not the content to generate; if no engine matches it, the compatible family remains available. Changes nothing on screen.

modelsSelect.title: Pick a model
modelsSelect.description: Arms a model for a generation family. The Generator’s form is then rebuilt on that model’s own fields.

generatorPrepare.title: Prepare a generation
generatorPrepare.description: Fills the Generator’s form with a model and its parameters, then shows it. Nothing is sent.

generatorReadArmedGeneration.title: Read what is armed
generatorReadArmedGeneration.description: Answers the Generator’s model, operation, sources and destination as it stands. Sends nothing and spends nothing.

generatorSubmit.title: Start the prepared generation
generatorSubmit.description: Sends the form as it stands. Spends on the account serving that model, and the estimate is stated first where there is one.

jobsList.title: List the jobs
jobsList.description: Returns the generations under way and how far along they are, as the studio tracks them. Changes nothing on screen.

promptSuggest.title: Suggest prompt variants
promptSuggest.description: Rewrites a sentence into several variants cut for the model armed in the Generator, with the settings that go with them. Spends nothing and changes nothing on screen.

promptTranslate.title: Translate a prompt into English
promptTranslate.description: Carries a text into the language the models are trained on, and says which language it recognised. Spends nothing and changes nothing on screen.

actionsFind.title: Find actions
actionsFind.description: Searches by keywords across every action the studio publishes and hands back the ones that match, with their fields. Changes nothing on screen. This is also what answers « what can you do about X »: search the word, then say what came back.

chatClose.title: Close the conversation
chatClose.description: Clears the conversation off the screen so the result can be seen. Call it last, and only once the result is there — never when the answer is the words themselves, nor while permission is being asked.

promptDescribeStyle.title: Describe the style of the references
promptDescribeStyle.description: Reads the reference images sitting on the Generator’s form and returns a description usable as a prompt. Spends nothing.

studioState.title: Read the studio’s state
studioState.description: Returns the open project, the active workspace and surface, every open document with the one in front marked, the model armed per family, and whether the studio is signed in. Ask this before firing a command: a command only reaches the surface that is active.

documentsList.title: List the project’s documents
documentsList.description: Returns the editable documents the project folder holds — layered images, scenes, edits, materials — open in a tab or not. The project’s other files, images and models included, are not here.

documentOpen.title: Open a document
documentOpen.description: Opens a document of the project folder by its path and brings it to the front, switching workspace as needed. The path is the one a listing gave.

documentActivate.title: Bring a document to the front
documentActivate.description: Makes an already open document the active tab, so that commands aimed at its surface reach it. This is the answer to a command refused for being on the wrong surface. Name it by its id, by its path, or by the title the studio shows in quotes — a title two documents share names neither. “Reopen X”, “go back to X” for a document already open is this, not file.open.

documentClose.title: Close a document
documentClose.description: Closes an open document’s tab. Work that never reached the disk is lost with it.

documentRename.title: Rename a document
documentRename.description: Calls a document something else, on disk and on screen at once. The document keeps its identity, so an open tab renames without closing.

documentSave.title: Save a document
documentSave.description: Writes the named document into the project and waits for it to land. Without an id, the one in front. Answers whether anything was written: an untouched tab has nothing to write, and that is not a failure.

documentDeleteFromDisk.title: Delete a document
documentDeleteFromDisk.description: Takes the document’s file out of the project, then closes its tab. Unsaved work goes with it: the file is leaving, and saving it before destroying it would mean nothing.

activityRecent.title: Read the recent activity
activityRecent.description: Returns what the studio has recorded lately — generations, file operations, failures — newest first. This is how to find out what an action actually did. How one generation WENT is job.readCloudGeneration, which answers it whole.

projectsList.title: List the recent projects
projectsList.description: Answers the recent projects in the order the studio shows them, each with the absolute path that opens it — pass that path to project.open.

projectOpen.title: Open a project folder
projectOpen.description: Opens a project from an absolute path on this machine, without raising the system dialogue a person would use. Answers whether the folder was a project.

projectClose.title: Close the open project
projectClose.description: Closes the open project and leaves the studio with none: every panel empties and the catalogue stops answering. The folder is untouched and stays among the recent projects.

projectCreate.title: Create a project folder
projectCreate.description: Makes a project and opens it, without raising the system dialogue a person would use. A NAME is enough — the studio puts it where this person keeps projects, named above. The folder field says which folder to make it in, when the sentence names one. To leave the place open to choice, call the action all the same: its confirmation carries a button that opens the system picker and fills the folder field.

projectForget.title: Drop a project from the recent ones
projectForget.description: Drops a project from the list of recent projects, which is a list of shortcuts and nothing more. THE FOLDER IS NOT TOUCHED and nothing is erased: reopening the project puts the row back. To put the folder in the trash, that is project.trash. Named by the absolute path projects.list answers.

projectTrash.title: Move a project to the trash
projectTrash.description: Moves the project FOLDER and everything in it — documents, assets, catalogue — to the system trash. Nothing in the studio undoes it: only the system trash can give it back. The project is closed if it was open, and its row leaves the recent projects. To drop the row alone without touching the folder, that is project.forget. Named by the absolute path projects.list answers.

fileOpen.title: Open a file of the project
fileOpen.description: Opens any file the project folder holds — an image, a 3D model, a material, a document — in the space that edits it, the way a double-click in the Explorer does. A file no editor here takes is handed to the program that owns it.

filesList.title: List a folder
filesList.description: Returns the entries of one folder of the open project, files and folders alike, with the path each is known by. Give no folder to list the project root.

filesSearch.title: Search the project’s files
filesSearch.description: Searches the whole open project by name and returns the matching entries with their paths. Changes nothing on screen. Finding is not opening: file.open opens what was found, and file.rename renames it.

filesMove.title: Move files
filesMove.description: Moves files and folders of the project into another folder of it. The disk changes, though the Explorer can still undo it afterwards.

filesCopy.title: Copy files
filesCopy.description: Copies files and folders of the project into another folder of it, leaving the originals where they are.

filesDuplicate.title: Duplicate files
filesDuplicate.description: Makes a copy of each named file or folder beside it, under a name the studio picks so nothing is overwritten.

filesTrash.title: Move files to the bin
filesTrash.description: Sends files and folders of the project to the system bin. What it took is listed in the recent activity.

fileRename.title: Rename a file
fileRename.description: Gives one file or folder of the project another name, in the folder it already sits in. Another program may already know it by the old one.

fileFacts.title: Read a file’s facts
fileFacts.description: Returns what the filesystem records about one entry — its kind, its size in bytes, when it was created and last changed. Changes nothing on screen.

folderNew.title: Create a folder
folderNew.description: Makes a new folder inside a folder of the open project. Answers with the path it was given, which may differ if the name was taken.

filesUndoFileOperation.title: Undo the last batch of file changes
filesUndoFileOperation.description: Takes back the last move, rename or duplication of project files. The stack lives in the main process and covers every window, but a trashing is not taken back.

filesRedoFileOperation.title: Redo the last batch of file changes
filesRedoFileOperation.description: Replays the batch of file changes that was just undone, exactly as the Explorer does. Answers with what moved and what was refused.

filesCanUndoRedo.title: Read the file undo stack
filesCanUndoRedo.description: Says whether undoing or redoing would do anything, without attempting either. It is what greys out the two menu rows before they are clicked.

fileReveal.title: Show a file in the system file manager
fileReveal.description: Opens the Finder or the system explorer on the named file, selected. The path never leaves the main process.

projectRename.title: Rename a project
projectRename.description: Renames a project, which MOVES its folder: a project is named by its folder and by nothing else. What it holds travels with it, and nothing is erased. Named by the absolute path projects.list answers, so a closed one can be renamed too — and the path answered is the NEW one.

modelsReadGenerationModelFields.title: Read a model’s own inputs
modelsReadGenerationModelFields.description: Returns the fields one generation model accepts, with their kinds and bounds, as the studio builds its form from. This is what to fill the parameters of a prepared generation with.

costEstimate.title: Estimate what a generation would cost
costEstimate.description: Prices a model and a set of parameters without running anything. Its parameters take the shape models_readGenerationModelFields answers with. Answers nothing at all where the API declines to price that model, rather than inventing a figure.

jobReadCloudGeneration.title: Read one job
jobReadCloudGeneration.description: Returns one generation whole — its status, how far along it is, what it produced, what it cost, and why it failed if it did. Asked for « the result of my last generation », this is what says how it WENT; the image or the 3D model it produced is in the project catalogue.

jobWaitForCloudGeneration.title: Wait for a job to finish
jobWaitForCloudGeneration.description: Waits until a generation succeeds, fails or is cancelled, then returns it with the assets it produced. Returns the job as it stands if the wait runs out, which is an answer rather than a failure.

jobCancelCloudGeneration.title: Cancel a job
jobCancelCloudGeneration.description: Stops a generation that is still queued or running. What has already been spent is not given back.

taskCancelLocalTask.title: Cancel a local task
taskCancelLocalTask.description: Stops a task the studio is running on this machine — a render, an import, an indexing pass — half-written file and all. Answers whether one was still running, which an id that already finished is not.

usageReport.title: Read the usage report
usageReport.description: Returns what the account has spent over a window of seven, thirty-one or a hundred and twenty days, as the usage window shows it. This is what answers « how many credits have I left ».

assetsSearchProjectCatalogue.title: Search the project’s catalogue
assetsSearchProjectCatalogue.description: Searches THIS project’s own catalogue, on this machine, by text, kind and tags, and can narrow to what was generated. The catalogue holds assets, not the project’s files: a file the person names is found by searching the project’s files. The account’s remote library is elsewhere again. What the catalogue holds ON one asset — where it came from, how it is tagged — is asset.get, on the ids this hands back.

assetsCounts.title: Count the project’s catalogue
assetsCounts.description: Returns how many images, videos, audio assets, 3D models, skyboxes and animations this project holds on this machine, counted in the catalogue rather than by listing them. Every kind is returned, including those whose count is zero.

assetGet.title: Read assets
assetGet.description: Returns everything the catalogue holds about the named assets — where they are, what they came from, and how they are tagged. This is what to call on the ids a finished generation handed back.

assetUpdate.title: Correct an asset
assetUpdate.description: Changes an asset’s name, its tags, or the kind the studio read from its extension. Tags are replaced whole, so an empty list genuinely clears them.

assetsRemoveFromLibrary.title: Remove assets
assetsRemoveFromLibrary.description: Takes assets out of the project’s library, and out of the remote one when asked to. What it removed is listed in the recent activity.

assetsCaptionImages.title: Caption images
assetsCaptionImages.description: Has the API read the named images and writes what it sees there as the asset’s name. Only images the library already knows can be captioned, so a purely local selection answers zero.

assetsListMissing.title: Find assets whose file has gone
assetsListMissing.description: Among the named assets, returns those the catalogue expects a file for that is no longer there. An asset that never had a local file is never one of them, since nothing was expected of it.

assetExtractTextures.title: Extract a model’s images
assetExtractTextures.description: Pulls the images a 3D file carries out of it and brings them into the project’s library as assets of their own. Returns the rows it has just created.

assetReveal.title: Show an asset in the system file manager
assetReveal.description: Opens the Finder or the system explorer on an asset’s file. An asset that lives only in the remote library has nothing to show, and says so.

canvasState.title: Read the image being edited
canvasState.description: Answers the image in front — its size, its resolution, its guides, and every layer of the stack flattened: id, name, kind, and what each carries. A field STANDING AT ITS DEFAULT is left out, and absent means that default: a layer is drawn, whole, unlocked, blended normally, uncut and untransformed.

animationReopenMotion.title: Reopen a character motion
animationReopenMotion.description: Replaces the animation workbench with the motion saved in an animation asset for the named model. The asset must carry motion data created by this studio.

aiLocalState.title: Read local AI runtime
aiLocalState.description: Returns local AI candidates, installed and loaded state, roles, machine fit, downloads and runtime readiness.

aiManageLocalRuntime.title: Manage local AI runtime
aiManageLocalRuntime.description: Chooses, installs, removes, loads or unloads a local AI candidate, or reads and repairs its runtime. Read ai.localState first. Every operation except reading the engine changes the studio and requires confirmation.

canvasSetDocumentProperties.title: Set image document properties
canvasSetDocumentProperties.description: Changes the print resolution, colour mode or bit depth of the image in front. Read canvas.state first; values not named stay unchanged.

canvasGenerationComment.title: Manage image generation comments
canvasGenerationComment.description: Adds, updates or removes an instruction for the next generation on the image in front. Coordinates and an optional polygon use document pixels. A layer id scopes a new note to that layer; without one it applies to the whole image. canvas.state returns pending comments and their identifiers.

canvasResize.title: Resize the image
canvasResize.description: Changes the frame of the image in front. Rescales the layers with it when asked to, and otherwise leaves them where they are, which is the difference between image size and canvas size.

canvasSetPixelArt.title: Set pixel art mode
canvasSetPixelArt.description: Puts the image in front on a pixel-art grid, or takes it off one. Given a count of columns and rows, resizes the document so the artwork measures exactly that in cells. 🛑 A resize drops the pixel history — strokes already laid stay, but ⌘Z no longer undoes them. Resizing and laying the grid are TWO undos: the first ⌘Z takes the grid off and leaves the size.

canvasDrawPixels.title: Draw pixels
canvasDrawPixels.description: Lays cells on the image in front, in one go and one undo — cells named one by one, a line, a rectangle filled or hollow, or a fill. Coordinates are in grid cells, not in document pixels.

canvasCrop.title: Crop the image
canvasCrop.description: Closes the frame onto a rectangle given in document coordinates. The layers keep their place, so what falls outside is what is cut away.

canvasFlipOrRotate.title: Flip or turn the image
canvasFlipOrRotate.description: Mirrors the image across an axis, or turns it a quarter turn either way. A turn swaps the frame’s width and height, so a portrait becomes a landscape.

layerSetMaskOptions.title: Set a layer’s mask
layerSetMaskOptions.description: Says whether a MASK — a shape carved out of a selection, which a layer wears — hides what it covers and whether it travels with the layer, or takes it off altogether. Hiding the layer ITSELF is layer.setOpacityBlendAndVisibility. A layer wearing no mask is refused: carving one belongs to the engine, through the command that makes one from the selection.

guideAdd.title: Lay a guide
guideAdd.description: Lays a vertical or a horizontal guide at the place given, in document coordinates, and answers the id it has just been given. The two actions beside it move it and take it away by that id.

guideMove.title: Move a guide
guideMove.description: Changes where a guide sits, in document coordinates, as a drag from the ruler would. An id nothing answers to is refused.

guideRemove.title: Remove a guide
guideRemove.description: Takes a guide off the image, as a drag that drops it back on its ruler does. Clearing every guide at once is a command of the registry, fired another way.

layerAdd.title: Add a layer
layerAdd.description: Puts a new pixel, text or adjustment layer on top of the stack of the image in front, and answers with the id it was given. An adjustment layer must name the dial it carries.

layerRemove.title: Remove a layer
layerRemove.description: Takes one layer out of the stack of the image in front. Undoes like any other edit of that document.

layerSelect.title: Arm a layer
layerSelect.description: Makes one layer the armed one, which is what the tools of the image workspace act on. This is a way of looking at the stack rather than an edit, so it adds nothing to the history.

layerRename.title: Rename a layer
layerRename.description: Calls one layer of the image in front something else. The id does not change, so nothing that referred to it is lost.

layerSetOpacityBlendAndVisibility.title: Set how a layer is composited
layerSetOpacityBlendAndVisibility.description: Changes a layer’s opacity, fill opacity, blend mode, visibility or clipping. Every field is optional, and what is not given is left exactly as it was. THIS is what hides a layer and shows it again — « masque ce calque » sets visible to false, and has nothing to do with a mask.

layerTransform.title: Move, scale or rotate a layer
layerTransform.description: Moves, scales or turns one layer inside the frame. The rotation is given in degrees, and every field left out keeps the value the layer already had.

layerEditTextLayer.title: Set a text layer’s words
layerEditTextLayer.description: Changes what a text layer says, the typeface and size it says it at, its colour, its alignment and its box. Refuses a layer that holds pixels rather than words, which the command would otherwise leave untouched.

layerReorderInStack.title: Reorder a layer
layerReorderInStack.description: Moves a layer to another place in the stack, and into or out of a group. Index zero is the bottom of the stack, which is what the eye sees last.

layerDuplicate.title: Duplicate a layer
layerDuplicate.description: Copies one layer just above itself, children included, every copy given a fresh id. Answers with the id of the copy. The image’s FILE is copied by files.duplicate; this copies one layer inside it.

layerGroup.title: Group layers
layerGroup.description: Gathers top-level layers into one group, which then moves as a whole. Answers with the group’s own id.

layerUngroup.title: Dissolve a group
layerUngroup.description: Takes a group apart, leaving its children where the group stood in the stack.

layerMergeDown.title: Merge a layer down
layerMergeDown.description: Folds one layer into the layer below it, within its own level of the stack. The result keeps the lower layer’s identity.

sequenceState.title: Read the edit being worked on
sequenceState.description: Answers the edit in front — its settings, its length, the playhead and what is selected — then every track with its clips, their bounds, their entry into the source, their speed, their fades and their level. A field STANDING AT ITS DEFAULT is left out, and absent means that default: a row is heard and unlocked, a clip runs at speed 1 from its start, with no fade and at the level it was recorded.

sequenceSeek.title: Place the playhead
sequenceSeek.description: Moves the playhead of the edit in front to the given instant, in microseconds. Not a change: nothing enters the history, and undo does not bring it back.

clipAdd.title: Lay a clip on the edit
clipAdd.description: Lays an asset from the library on a track of the edit in front, at the given instant or under the playhead. Opens the tracks it needs, and links a take’s image to its sound when it carries one.

clipRemove.title: Take a clip off the edit
clipRemove.description: Removes a clip from its track, and the half linked to it with it. The room it took stays empty rather than closing over its neighbours.

clipMove.title: Move a clip
clipMove.description: Carries a clip to a given track and instant, overwriting whatever sits there. A locked track, or one of another kind, takes nothing.

clipTrim.title: Trim one edge of a clip
clipTrim.description: Pulls a clip’s in or out point to the given instant, never past the source behind it. A still has no source to run past and stretches freely. “at” is an instant on the TIMELINE and never a length: to make a clip two seconds longer, read its “end” and send that plus 2000000.

clipSplit.title: Cut a clip in two
clipSplit.description: Cuts a clip at the given instant and leaves both halves end to end. An instant outside the clip has nothing to cut, and is refused rather than reported as done.

clipFade.title: Set a clip’s fade
clipFade.description: Gives a CLIP’s fade in or fade out the length asked for, so a video or audio edit has to be in front. Two ramps longer than the clip itself are brought back to what it can carry. For a fade in a 3D scene’s cinematic, that is timeline.addSceneCue.

clipGain.title: Set a clip’s level
clipGain.description: Changes a clip’s level in decibels, zero leaving the take as it was recorded. The value is bounded to what playback can hold.

clipSpeed.title: Set a clip’s speed
clipSpeed.description: Changes how fast a clip plays, one being its original speed. Its length on the edit follows, the source it reads staying the same.

clipUnlink.title: Part an image from its sound
clipUnlink.description: Separates the two halves of a take, so that moving, trimming or cutting one no longer reaches the other. Nothing ties them back together afterwards.

clipSelect.title: Point at a clip
clipSelect.description: Names the clip the inspector and the gestures that aim at nothing will act on. Not a change, and undo does not take it back.

trackAdd.title: Add a track
trackAdd.description: Opens an image or sound track below the others. An image track can carry nothing of a sound, and the reverse holds too.

trackRemove.title: Remove a track
trackRemove.description: Takes a track off the edit, and every clip it carried with it. A locked track is not removed.

trackReorderTracks.title: Reorder the tracks
trackReorderTracks.description: Moves a track by the given number of rows, which changes what covers what. The rows are counted from the TOP, so a negative number moves it up and a positive one down — sequence.state answers them in that order, the first being the topmost.

trackRename.title: Rename a track
trackRename.description: Gives a track the name the header column shows. Its identifier never changes.

trackSetMuteSoloLockHeight.title: Set how a track is worked
trackSetMuteSoloLockHeight.description: Changes a track’s mute, solo, lock or height. Those four say how one works rather than what one made, and so never enter the history.

skyboxState.title: Read the sky being edited
skyboxState.description: Answers the sky in front — its equirectangular source, its image settings, where its sun sits and what colour it is, and what its environment lights — plus what produced it when it came from a generation.

skyboxSetViewportOptions.title: Set how a sky is looked at
skyboxSetViewportOptions.description: Chooses the projection the sky is drawn under, how wide the lens opens, and whether the test objects stand in it. It is session state, as every way of looking at a document is, and none of it is saved.

skyboxAdjustImage.title: Adjust a sky’s image
skyboxAdjustImage.description: Changes exposure, contrast, saturation, temperature, tint, horizon rotation or blur. Every field is optional, and what is not given is left as it was.

skyboxResetAdjustments.title: Bring the image settings back to neutral
skyboxResetAdjustments.description: Returns every image setting of the sky to its neutral value at once, in a single history entry. The source and the sun are left alone.

skyboxSetSun.title: Place and set the sun
skyboxSetSun.description: Changes the elevation, azimuth, intensity or colour of the sun in the sky in front. Both angles are in radians, as everywhere else in the scene.

skyboxSetPreviewLighting.title: Set what the sky lights
skyboxSetPreviewLighting.description: Changes how strongly the sky lights the test objects, and decides whether the image is drawn behind them or merely lights them.

skyboxSetSourceImage.title: Choose a sky’s image
skyboxSetSourceImage.description: Hangs an equirectangular image from the library in the sky in front. The asset must have a file on this machine, one still in the cloud having nothing to decode.

materialState.title: Read the material being edited
materialState.description: Answers the material in front — the eight channels and what fills them, every render setting such as colour, roughness and tiling, and how the preview is presented.

materialSetSurfaceSettings.title: Set a material
materialSetSurfaceSettings.description: Changes the tint, roughness, metalness, relief, occlusion, emission, tiling, offset or rotation of the material in front. Every field is optional.

materialSetPreviewEnvironment.title: Choose what lights a material preview
materialSetPreviewEnvironment.description: Lights the preview by the procedural studio, by an image of the project named by its asset identifier, or by a sky document named by its title — the preview then takes its graded image and its intensity, as a scene does.

materialSetPreviewDisplay.title: Set a material’s preview
materialSetPreviewDisplay.description: Changes the strength and rotation of the environment lighting the preview, whether the background is drawn, the automatic spin and the seam highlight.

materialSetChannelImage.title: Fill or empty a channel
materialSetChannelImage.description: Puts an image from the library into one of the eight channels of the material in front. With no asset named, the channel is emptied rather than filled.

documentExport.title: Export the document in front into the project
documentExport.description: Writes the document in front — image, scene, sky, material or edit — into a folder of the project, named after its title when none is given. An edit comes out as OpenTimelineIO, the cut rather than a film, the frame-by-frame render needing a session nothing outside can hold. The destination cannot leave the project.

gitStashDrop.title: Throw a shelved change away
gitStashDrop.description: Removes a shelved change from the stack without applying it back. What it held was never recorded, so nothing gives it back.

gitResolve.title: Settle a merge conflict
gitResolve.description: Keeps one of the two sides of a conflict for the files named. What the other side held is gone from the working copy.

gitAbortMerge.title: Abandon the merge in progress
gitAbortMerge.description: Brings the repository back to where it stood before the merge, undoing what it had already written into the working copy.

gitRemotes.title: List the remote repositories
gitRemotes.description: Answers the remotes declared, with their name and their address. It is where a push would go.

gitAddRemote.title: Declare a remote repository
gitAddRemote.description: Adds a remote under the name given. Nothing is sent or fetched by this alone, which writes to the local configuration.

gitFetch.title: Fetch the remote references
gitFetch.description: Reads where the remote repository stands, changing nothing in your working copy and publishing nothing. It is the harmless half of a pull.

gitPull.title: Fetch and merge
gitPull.description: Fetches the remote and merges into the current branch, which rewrites the working copy. A conflict stops there and is settled afterwards. Asked only for what the remote holds, this is the wrong call: git.fetch reads it without touching the working copy.

gitPush.title: Publish to the remote repository
gitPush.description: Sends the current branch to the remote repository. It is the only gesture of the studio that leaves this machine, and nothing here takes it back.

cloudBrowseAccountLibrary.title: Browse the remote library
cloudBrowseAccountLibrary.description: Answers one page of the account’s library, narrowed by text, tags or kind. Paging is by cursor, and there is no total — the API gives none.

cloudExplorePublicFeed.title: Browse what everyone published
cloudExplorePublicFeed.description: Answers one page of the public feed of a given kind, newest first. These assets are not yours, and looking at them fetches none of them. cloud.pull is what brings one down into the project, bytes and all.

cloudFindSimilarPublished.title: Find what resembles an asset
cloudFindSimilarPublished.description: Answers published assets that resemble the one named, that one taken out of its own results. The reference is the caller’s to choose.

cloudPreviewSync.title: See what a synchronisation would do
cloudPreviewSync.description: Says what a push or a pull would do to each asset named, before it costs a single request. Nothing is sent and nothing is fetched.

cloudPull.title: Fetch remote assets
cloudPull.description: Brings assets into the project, bytes and all, and says what each one did. A download that stops halfway keeps what it had already written.

cloudPush.title: Send assets to the account
cloudPush.description: Sends local assets up to the account’s library, where they stay. It is the only gesture of this family that leaves something behind.

stylesList.title: List the material styles
stylesList.description: Answers the saved material styles, with their identifier, their name and the values they keep. They live outside every project and follow the machine.

styleSave.title: Save the material as a style
styleSave.description: Records the material of the document in front under the given name. The name is a base, the studio making it unique when it is already taken.

styleRename.title: Rename a material style
styleRename.description: Gives a saved style its name. Nothing else about the style moves, and its identifier stays the same.

styleRemove.title: Delete a material style
styleRemove.description: Removes a saved style. It lives outside every project, so nothing gives it back — neither undo nor the Explorer.

authState.title: Tell whether the studio is signed in
authState.description: Says whether an API key is in place and which account the studio works on. Never answers the key itself, which does not leave the main process.

windowState.title: Read the state of the window
windowState.description: Answers the size of the window, whether it is maximised or full screen, and the language it draws in — the one the main process actually settled on.

windowFullScreen.title: Toggle full screen
windowFullScreen.description: Takes the window into full screen, or out of it. It is a toggle, and there is no way to ask for one of the two states.

settingsOpen.title: Open the settings on a section
settingsOpen.description: Opens the settings window on the section asked for, or brings it there when it is already up. Reading and writing a setting does not need it opened.

updatesState.title: Read where the update stands
updatesState.description: Says where the application update stands — nothing in sight, downloading, or ready to install on the next quit. updates.install is what installs it and restarts the studio.

mediaCapabilities.title: Tell what the studio can decode
mediaCapabilities.description: Says what this machine is capable of on the media side, which depends on ffmpeg being there. Without it importing still works and the interface says what it cannot do.

mediaIndexFileInPlace.title: Give a file a catalogue row
mediaIndexFileInPlace.description: Brings a file the project folder already holds into the catalogue, without copying it. It is the half of importing that raises no system dialogue.

fontsList.title: List the installed fonts
fontsList.description: Answers the typefaces a text can be set in, the ones that ship with the studio first, then the ones installed on this machine. Each comes with where it is from, which setting a face needs as much as its name.

favoritesListPinnedRecipes.title: List the pinned recipes
favoritesListPinnedRecipes.description: Answers the recipes pinned to the project, with the model that produced them and the workspace that knows how to make them again. A recipe keeps enough to start a generation over.

favoritePinAssetRecipe.title: Pin what produced an asset
favoritePinAssetRecipe.description: Pins what produced an asset of the open project, so it can be made again. An asset nobody generated has no recipe to keep.

favoriteUnpinAssetRecipe.title: Remove a pinned recipe
favoriteUnpinAssetRecipe.description: Takes a recipe off the pinned list. The asset it had produced is left alone.

fileInfoOpenWindow.title: Open a file’s information
fileInfoOpenWindow.description: Opens the window describing a file of the project — its size, its kind, its history and what the catalogue knows of it.

mirrorOpenVideoReturnWindow.title: Open the video return
mirrorOpenVideoReturnWindow.description: Opens the return window, or brings it to the front when it is already there. It shows what the edit plays, and carries none of the editing.

helpOpenStudioWindow.title: Open a studio window
helpOpenStudioWindow.description: Opens the user manual, the licences window, the usage window, the journal or the welcome — or brings it to the front if it is already there. These are windows of the main process, and no command of the registry reaches them.

updatesInstall.title: Install the downloaded update
updatesInstall.description: Quits the studio and relaunches the version already downloaded. Only does anything once the update is ready, and whatever is unsaved goes with the quit.

dictationState.title: Read the dictation state
dictationState.description: Says where speech recognition stands — idle, listening, waiting on a permission or on a model — and what failed if anything did.

dictationStart.title: Start dictation
dictationStart.description: Opens the microphone and writes what it hears wherever the caret is. With no field focused dictation has nowhere to write, so the caret is placed before the call.

dictationStop.title: Stop dictating
dictationStop.description: Closes the microphone. Keeps what was heard by default, and can throw it away instead — that is exactly where the two gestures differ.

panelsList.title: List the panels
panelsList.description: Returns the panels the surface in front can show, and says which ones are up. A panel that surface does not serve is not listed, since it cannot be opened there.

panelOpen.title: Open a panel
panelOpen.description: Brings a panel forward, in the place the surface in front reserves for it. A panel already up is focused rather than rewritten.

panelClose.title: Close a panel
panelClose.description: Clears the half the surface in front keeps that panel in. The arrangement of the other panels does not move.

sceneState.title: Read the scene being edited
sceneState.description: Returns every object of the 3D document in front — its id, name, type, parent, visibility and transform, with the geometry, material or light it carries — plus what is selected, the camera shots, and the setting of the scene. A field STANDING AT ITS DEFAULT is left out, and absent means that default: no parent, drawn, standing at the origin unturned and unscaled, the studio’s own colour, a shape divided as its own kind always is. Measurements are never left out. A list that holds nothing is left out whole. To describe ONE object with its components and what may still be added to it, studio.describe.

optimizationAnalyze.title: Analyse scene optimisation
optimizationAnalyze.description: Returns the deterministic optimisation plan for the named objects, or for the whole scene when none are named. It changes nothing.

optimizationSelection.title: Optimise selection
optimizationSelection.description: Sets the selected objects to automatic SAFE runtime optimisation while keeping every authoring object editable.

optimizationWorld.title: Optimise the scene
optimizationWorld.description: Sets every object to automatic SAFE runtime optimisation while keeping the authoring scene unchanged.

optimizationReport.title: Read the optimisation report
optimizationReport.description: Returns measured scene costs separately from estimated SAFE runtime gains.

optimizationClearCache.title: Clear the optimisation cache
optimizationClearCache.description: Discards the scene viewport’s disposable optimised representation so it is rebuilt from authoring state.

optimizationExclude.title: Exclude objects from optimisation
optimizationExclude.description: Keeps the named logical objects individual in optimised rendering.

optimizationSetMode.title: Set object optimisation mode
optimizationSetMode.description: Sets Auto, Force Individual, Force Instance, Force Batch or Exclude on the named objects.

nodeAdd.title: Add an object to the scene
nodeAdd.description: Puts a primitive, a light, a camera, a sprite or a text into the 3D document in front, at the position given. Answers with the id the object was born with. A model of the project, or the one a generation has just answered, comes in through node.addModel; this makes a primitive.

nodeAddModel.title: Place a model from the library
nodeAddModel.description: Puts a 3D model of the project’s library into the scene in front, named by its asset. This is how a generated mesh gets into a scene.

nodeRemove.title: Remove an object
nodeRemove.description: Takes one object out of the scene in front, with whatever hangs from it. Undoes like any other edit of that document.

nodeRename.title: Rename an object
nodeRename.description: Calls one object of the scene in front something else. The id does not change, so nothing that pointed at it is lost.

nodeAttach.title: Hang an object on a character
nodeAttach.description: Hangs an object on the attachment point of the character it belongs to — a sword in a hand. With no point named, the object follows the whole character.

nodeTransform.title: Place an object
nodeTransform.description: Moves, turns or scales one object. Rotations are Euler angles in radians, and every axis left out keeps the value the object already had.

nodeSetVisible.title: Show or hide an object
nodeSetVisible.description: Takes one object out of what is drawn, or puts it back. It stays in the scene either way, which is what tells hiding from removing.

nodeSetMeshMaterial.title: Set an object’s material
nodeSetMeshMaterial.description: Changes the colour, roughness, metalness, tiling density and five maps of a mesh or a text. A slot named with an empty id is a map taken off. Tiling is refused on a text, whose outline is not a primitive.

nodeSetPrimitiveParameters.title: Set the parameters of a primitive
nodeSetPrimitiveParameters.description: Changes the measurements and segment counts of the shape a mesh was built from. Each primitive carries its own, which reading the scene hands over — a field that does not belong to the shape is refused rather than ignored.

nodeSetShadowCastAndReceive.title: Set an object’s shadows
nodeSetShadowCastAndReceive.description: Says whether an object throws a shadow and whether it catches the ones others throw. A light catches none, a sprite does neither, and the field the object cannot hold is refused.

nodeSetSpriteSettings.title: Set a sprite
nodeSetSpriteSettings.description: Changes the tint, the opacity and the image of a sprite, which always faces the camera. An empty id takes the image off and leaves the plain coloured quad.

nodeSetTextSettings.title: Set a 3D text
nodeSetTextSettings.description: Changes the words, the typeface, the size, the depth out of its own plane and the curve fineness of a text. Its material is set through the material action, like a mesh’s.

nodeSetPathShape.title: Set the shape of a rail
nodeSetPathShape.description: Changes the tension of a rail, from 0 angular to 1 round, and whether it closes back on itself. Its control points are added, moved and dropped by the three actions beside this one.

pathAddPoint.title: Add a point to a rail
pathAddPoint.description: Lays a control point. With coordinates, it is added past the last one, where it was aimed. With an index, it is slipped just after that point, halfway to its neighbour. With neither, it extends the rail off its end.

pathMovePoint.title: Move a point of a rail
pathMovePoint.description: Changes the coordinates of a control point, in the rail’s own frame — so moving the rail moves the whole trajectory. An index naming no point is refused.

pathRemovePoint.title: Remove a point from a rail
pathRemovePoint.description: Drops a control point. A rail never falls below two points, one point being no line, and the call is refused there.

modelSetMaterialDocument.title: Dress a model in a material
modelSetMaterialDocument.description: Makes an imported model wear a material of the project, named by the title of its document. The model then follows that material, so editing one of its channels or dials repaints it, with nothing asked here again. An empty title takes it off, and the model goes back to what its own file carries.

nodeSetLightSettings.title: Set a light
nodeSetLightSettings.description: Changes everything the kind of light in hand carries — its colour, intensity, range, decay, the width and softness of its cone, its target, and the two colours of a hemisphere light. A field the kind does not carry is refused. A glow, a bloom or any other effect is not a light: post.set writes one parameter of an effect and post.reset puts it back.

nodeSetCameraLens.title: Set a camera lens
nodeSetCameraLens.description: Changes the field of view and the near and far distances of a camera. Where it stands is set by its transform, like anything else in the tree.

cameraAddShot.title: Put a camera on air
cameraAddShot.description: Opens a shot for this camera, from the given instant in seconds, and answers its id. Which line it lands on follows the band’s own rule, where a camera not yet on the band arrives on top. A camera with a shot is the ACTIVE camera, the one the scene is seen through.

cameraBindPathToShot.title: Run a camera along a path
cameraBindPathToShot.description: Binds a path to the named shot: the camera travels it for the whole of the shot, at a steady speed along its length. With no path, the shot no longer moves the camera. A start past the end runs the path backwards.

cameraCreateAndBindPath.title: Lay a rail under a camera
cameraCreateAndBindPath.description: Makes a rail where the camera stands, aimed down its line of sight, and binds it to the shot in one gesture. The action beside it binds a rail that already exists; this one makes it, because a rail drives nothing without a shot to run it.

cameraReorder.title: Move a camera’s line on the band
cameraReorder.description: Takes a camera’s line up or down, which settles what the film looks through where two shots overlap. The number is a count of rows, negative to go down, and the answer says how far the line could actually move.

cameraAimShotAt.title: Give a camera something to aim at
cameraAimShotAt.description: Aims the camera of the named shot at an object — which it follows even when animated — or at a fixed point. With neither, the camera stays aimed by its own rotation alone.

nodeReparent.title: Reparent an object
nodeReparent.description: Hangs one object under another, or under the scene itself when no parent is given, and puts it where asked among its new neighbours. Giving a place without a parent therefore lifts the object up to the scene: repeat the parent to change nothing but the place. The object keeps its own transform, which is then read relative to its new parent.

nodeSelect.title: Select objects
nodeSelect.description: Makes these objects the selection the inspector reads and the gizmo moves. Selection is not an edit, so it adds nothing to the history.

viewDirection.title: Look at the scene from one side
viewDirection.description: Puts the main view’s camera above, below, in front of, behind, to the left or to the right of the scene. It is a move, so it adds nothing to the history.

rigState.title: Read a character’s skeleton
rigState.description: Returns a model’s bones with their roles, the handles its joints reach for, the blocks laid on its band, and what the engine measured of the mesh.

rigFit.title: Make a model animatable
rigFit.description: Puts on the mesh the skeleton the studio fits to what it measured of it. Refuses while the engine has not read the model, which is a wait rather than a fault.

rigClear.title: Take a model’s skeleton off
rigClear.description: Returns the model to being a mesh, with no bones and no handles. The gesture undoes like every other one of the scene.

rigConfigureHands.title: Add the finger bones
rigConfigureHands.description: Puts the thirty finger bones at rest on whatever hands the skeleton already holds. With no hands recognised, nothing is written.

socketAdd.title: Lay an attachment point
socketAdd.description: Lays a point on a bone of the character in front that an object of a scene can follow — a hand, a back. The point lives in the character’s file.

socketRemove.title: Remove an attachment point
socketRemove.description: Removes an attachment point from the character in front. Whatever followed it falls back onto the character itself.

boneAdd.title: Add a bone
boneAdd.description: Hangs a bone under the one named, resting exactly on it — the gizmo is what puts it where it belongs. Its name is composed from the parent’s.

boneRemove.title: Remove a bone
boneRemove.description: Takes a bone out of the skeleton and hangs its children where it hung: an elbow leaves, the hand stays.

boneRename.title: Rename a bone
boneRename.description: Changes a bone’s name, its children following on their own. A name already taken is refused rather than half written.

boneSetRole.title: Say which joint a bone IS
boneSetRole.description: Ties a bone to one of the joints of the humanoid standard, or to none when the role is left out. Whatever bone held that role loses it in the same move.

ikAdd.title: Put a handle on a joint
ikAdd.description: Adds a handle a joint reaches for, and the chain that follows it — the two bones above turn to come along, which is what puts a foot on the ground or a hand on a grip.

ikRemove.title: Remove a handle
ikRemove.description: Takes a chain and the handle it reached for, both: a handle left behind would be a bone nothing drives.

animationsList.title: List what a character can play
animationsList.description: Answers the three places a motion comes from — the clips the model’s own file carries, the animations shipped with the studio, and the ones the project library keeps. This is what answers « what animations does this scene carry »; the keys a band holds are read with scene.state instead.

animationAddBlock.title: Lay an animation block
animationAddBlock.description: Lays on a character’s band a motion from one of the three sources. The id names an asset of the library, the name names the two others, and exactly one of them belongs to a call. The band is made if the character had none.

animationSetBlockSettings.title: Set an animation block
animationSetBlockSettings.description: Changes where a block sits on the band, where playback starts inside the motion, its speed, its looping, the length of its fades, what it does with the movement of the root, and the part of the body it drives. The block is rewritten in place, every other lane left untouched.

animationRemoveBlock.title: Take an animation block off
animationRemoveBlock.description: Removes a block from the band, wherever it sat. The band stays, empty if it has to.

animationSetBandLengthAndRate.title: Set the animation band
animationSetBandLengthAndRate.description: Changes the band’s length, its rate in frames per second, or both. Whatever is not named is left alone.

animationAutoKey.title: Turn automatic keying on
animationAutoKey.description: Decides whether moving a bone writes a key as it goes. It is session state, as every way of looking at a scene is, and none of it is saved with the document.

keyWritePoseKeys.title: Key a subject
keyWritePoseKeys.description: Writes a key on every channel of an object or a bone, at the instant given or at the playhead, holding the pose shown at the playhead — the one node.transform placed. On an animated object node.transform keys the playhead itself, so to pose another instant: write the key there first, then place the object with the playhead on it. The channels it lacks are opened on the way, since demanding a track first would be asking for the thing already standing in the viewport.

keyRemoveSubjectKeys.title: Take a subject’s keys off
keyRemoveSubjectKeys.description: Takes back the key every channel of an object or a bone holds at that instant. Without this a pose would be one nobody could undo, and nothing else in the panel removes one.

keyWriteKeysOnOpenChannels.title: Key everything animated
keyWriteKeysOnOpenChannels.description: Writes a key on every channel the scene has already opened, at the instant given or at the playhead. It opens none, which is what tells this apart from keying one subject.

keyMove.title: Move a key
keyMove.description: Slides a key along its channel, keeping its value. A key landing on an instant another already holds replaces it, two keys on one frame being a state no playback could read back.

channelRemove.title: Remove an animation channel
channelRemove.description: Takes a channel away, and the keys it carried with it. A locked channel is refused rather than silently left standing.

channelSetMuteSoloLock.title: Set a channel’s flags
channelSetMuteSoloLock.description: Mutes a channel, plays it alone, or locks it. It is how one WORKS rather than a change to the document, so nothing is added to the history.

viewSetDisplayMode.title: Choose how the scene is drawn
viewSetDisplayMode.description: Switches the main view to shaded, wireframe, material-only or one of the other ways of drawing. The menu command only cycles from one to the next; this one names which.

sceneCapture.title: Take a still of the 3D view
sceneCapture.description: Writes a still of what the view shows into the project’s images, at the size asked for. The framing never changes — only the pixel count does, or the capture would show something other than the screen.

worldApplyPreset.title: Apply a ready-made world
worldApplyPreset.description: Sets the lighting, the backdrop, the haze and the grading of a scene in one call, for a kind of look. Each one writes only the fields it is about and leaves the rest as they were, so a ground somebody turned on stays on.

layerLock.title: Lock a layer
layerLock.description: Sets or lifts the three padlocks of a layer, the one on its pixels, the one on its place and the one on its transparency. They stop the hand on the canvas; a value written by another action goes through, as it does from the panels.

layerEditShapeLayer.title: Repaint a shape
layerEditShapeLayer.description: Changes the fill, the outline, the stroke width and the number of sides of a shape already drawn, without drawing it again. Taking away the fill and the outline at once is refused, as it would leave nothing to see.

layerSetAdjustmentAmount.title: Set an adjustment layer
layerSetAdjustmentAmount.description: Moves the one dial an adjustment layer carries — exposure, contrast, saturation or temperature. Naming any dial other than its own is refused rather than quietly dropped on the floor.

worldSetSceneLighting.title: Choose what lights the scene
worldSetSceneLighting.description: Lights the scene by the procedural studio, by an image of the project named by its asset identifier, or by a sky document named by its title — the scene then takes its graded image, its sun and its intensity. Also sets how strong that lighting is and how far it is turned about the vertical, laid over what the sky says.

worldSetBackground.title: Choose what hangs behind the scene
worldSetBackground.description: Puts the environment itself behind the scene, a flat colour, or nothing at all — the last leaving the background transparent, which is what a capture meant to be laid over something else needs.

worldSetFog.title: Set the haze of the scene
worldSetFog.description: Turns the haze off, fades it between two distances, or thickens it with depth. The colour and the distances belong to the shape that was chosen, and are left exactly as they were otherwise.

worldSetGroundPlane.title: Set the ground of the scene
worldSetGroundPlane.description: Shows or hides the ground the scene owns, and sets its colour, its side, its opacity and whether shadows land on it. This is how a ground is ADDED to a scene: a plane added as an object is scenery, not the ground. That ground belongs to the document, unlike the grid, which is a setting of the application.

worldSetLayers.title: Replace terrain and scatter entries
worldSetLayers.description: Replaces the scene’s durable terrain and scatter entry list with a complete validated list. Use scene.state to read the current entries before changing one.

worldSetToneMapping.title: Set how the scene is rendered
worldSetToneMapping.description: Chooses how high dynamic range is brought down to the screen, and by how many stops it is exposed. Both belong to the document rather than to the window that happens to be looking at it.

gitStatus.title: Read the repository version status
gitStatus.description: Returns the branch, what it tracks, how far ahead or behind it is, and every changed file with the half of git it sits in. Also says when the project has no repository at all. What changed INSIDE a file is git.diff; this only names the files.

gitLog.title: Read the history
gitLog.description: Returns a page of recorded versions, newest first, across every branch, with the names that point at each one. What changed inside a file between two versions is git.diff.

gitListCommitFiles.title: Read what a version changed
gitListCommitFiles.description: Returns the files one recorded version touched, and how each was touched — added, changed, removed or renamed.

gitDiff.title: Read what changed in a file
gitDiff.description: Returns the change inside one file, within a recorded version, or against the last one when no version is named.

gitBranches.title: List the branches
gitBranches.description: Returns every branch of the project’s repository, saying which one is checked out.

gitStashes.title: List the shelved changes
gitStashes.description: Returns what has been shelved, newest first, so a client can put one back by its place in the list.

gitInit.title: Start recording versions
gitInit.description: Runs git init on the open project and writes its ignore file, then answers the state it left. Does nothing to a project already recording.

gitStage.title: Stage files
gitStage.description: Moves changes into what the next recorded version will hold. Answers with the state it left, so nothing needs reading back.

gitUnstage.title: Unstage files
gitUnstage.description: Takes changes back out of what the next recorded version will hold, leaving the files themselves untouched.

gitRestore.title: Discard changes to files
gitRestore.description: Puts files back the way the last recorded version has them. What was never recorded is gone, and no undo in the studio reaches it.

gitCommit.title: Record a version
gitCommit.description: Records what is staged, under a message. Can amend the last version instead of adding one, which rewrites it rather than following it.

gitCreateBranch.title: Create a branch
gitCreateBranch.description: Starts a branch at the current version and moves onto it. The working tree is left exactly as it stands.

gitCheckout.title: Switch branch
gitCheckout.description: Moves onto another branch, rewriting the working tree to match it. A document open in a tab is then a document whose file changed under it.

gitStash.title: Shelve the current changes
gitStash.description: Shelves the working tree’s changes and returns it to the last recorded version. It takes the changes off the disk.

gitStashPop.title: Bring shelved changes back
gitStashPop.description: Puts one set of shelved changes back into the working tree and drops it from the shelf. It rewrites files.

gitTag.title: Tag a version
gitTag.description: Puts a name on one recorded version, so it can be found again without its hash.

settingsRead.title: Read the settings
settingsRead.description: Answers { settings, choices }: every setting the studio holds under settings, section by section, and under choices what each setting with a fixed list accepts, with its title and help. What the viewport DRAWS lives here — the grid, the shadows, the helpers — and so do the units, the theme and the language. No scene action turns any of them on.

settingsWrite.title: Change the settings
settingsWrite.description: Writes one or more settings, section by section. This is how the grid and the shadows are turned on or set — read them first, since a change that names nothing the studio knows is refused rather than written blind. What is not named is left alone.

accountsList.title: List the accounts
accountsList.description: Returns the generation accounts this studio holds, saying which one is active and which may be renamed or removed. No key or secret is ever returned.

accountsActivate.title: Switch account
accountsActivate.description: Makes one of the held accounts the one the studio generates through. Everything sent from then on goes out with its credentials.

accountsRename.title: Rename an account
accountsRename.description: Changes the label an account appears under in the studio. Neither the key nor the secret crosses this boundary, in either direction.

settingsTriggerAction.title: Press a settings button
settingsTriggerAction.description: Fires one of the buttons of the settings window — show a file, open the developer tools, copy the connection command, install the bridge, reset everything. The last two leave something behind and are asked about on screen.

contextReadProjectCards.title: Read the project’s context
contextReadProjectCards.description: Answers the context cards — what the PERSON has said this project is — with their title, their text and whether they apply.

contextWriteProjectCard.title: Write a context card
contextWriteProjectCard.description: Writes what the PERSON says the project IS or AIMS AT, as a whole, as a standing card read back every turn. A working rule about how a thing is done here — how cameras move, how files are named — is a memory instead (memory.write).

contextDeleteProjectCard.title: Delete a context card
contextDeleteProjectCard.description: Takes the card an id names out of the project’s context — what the person said, unsaid. Its text is lost.

targetSelect.title: Aim at a target
targetSelect.description: Points at what the next step will act on in the open document — a layer, a scene object, a clip. Take the identifier from the target list in this briefing; without that list there is nothing to aim at.

nodeMarkAsCuttingTool.title: Mark objects as tools
nodeMarkAsCuttingTool.description: Marks objects of the scene in front, or takes the mark off with “negative” FALSE: a marked object is CUT OUT of the others at the next fold, whichever fold is asked for and whatever the order of the ids. With no mark, the biggest shape is the matter.

nodeCombineIntoSolid.title: Carve, join or intersect objects
nodeCombineIntoSolid.description: Folds several objects of the scene in front into a single solid. THE ORDER OF THE IDS DOES NOT MATTER: the matter is the biggest shape unless matterId names it, and an object marked through node.markAsCuttingTool is always a tool. The original shapes are kept inside the solid and node.separate gives them back. Answers with the id of the solid. “intersect” keeps only the part where they overlap.

nodeSwapSolidMatterAndTool.title: Flip a fold
nodeSwapSolidMatterAndTool.description: Folds a solid of the scene in front the other way round: what had been carved becomes the matter, and the matter becomes the tool. For the fold that ran backwards, with no undo.

nodeSeparate.title: Separate a solid
nodeSeparate.description: Breaks apart a solid of the scene in front and gives back the shapes it was made of, each where it stood. Answers with the ids of the objects handed back.

modelSetBaseColorImage.title: Cover a model with an image
modelSetBaseColorImage.description: Puts one image of the project over a whole imported model, as its base colour — the simple way to dress it. It excludes materials: a model covered with an image wears none, and the other way round. No other channel is derived from it. With no image, the dress comes off and the model goes back to what its own file carries.

postState.title: Read the post-processing composition
postState.description: Returns the stack of effects the scene — or the named camera — films through, with the id of each instance, which effect it is, its parameters, whether it is on, and whether the chain leaves it out.

postAdd.title: Add a post-processing effect
postAdd.description: Puts an effect from the catalogue at the end of the stack, on its own defaults. With no camera named it is the scene’s composition that receives it, the one the viewport already shows.

postRemove.title: Remove a post-processing effect
postRemove.description: Takes an instance out of the stack, and with it the timeline channels that drove it — left behind, they would aim at an effect nothing can reach any more.

postMove.title: Move an effect within the stack
postMove.description: Changes where an instance sits in the chain, which changes the image obtained — a grade before a bloom does not give the same result as a grade after it.

postSet.title: Set one parameter of an effect
postSet.description: Writes a value onto one parameter of an instance, held to the bounds the catalogue declares for that parameter. Which field to fill depends on its nature — a number, a switch or a word.

postSetEffectEnabled.title: Switch one effect on or off
postSetEffectEnabled.description: Turns an instance off without removing it, which takes it out of the computation and not merely out of the image. Its parameters stay where they are, ready to be turned back on.

postSetWholeStackEnabled.title: Switch the whole composition off
postSetWholeStackEnabled.description: Turns the entire stack off or back on in one go, losing nothing — the Before/After, as a value of the document that undo can take back.

postApplyPreset.title: Apply a post-processing preset
postApplyPreset.description: Replaces the stack with a ready-made composition — a set of effects, in an order, on values that agree with one another. The document receives the stack itself, never a reference to the preset.

postSetCameraStackMode.title: Say what a camera does with post-processing
postSetCameraStackMode.description: Chooses whether this camera follows the scene’s composition, carries its own, or applies none at all. Moving it to its own starts it from what it was already filming.

postListPresets.title: List the post-processing presets
postListPresets.description: Answers the ready-made compositions the studio ships and the ones saved on this machine, by name. This is the list post.applyPreset accepts.

postDuplicate.title: Duplicate a post-processing effect
postDuplicate.description: Puts a copy of the effect right after it, on the same values and under a fresh identity. Refused for an effect a second instance of means nothing — an anti-aliaser, an occlusion.

postReset.title: Reset a post-processing effect
postReset.description: Brings every parameter of that effect back to what the catalogue declares, without taking it out of the stack or moving it.

postAddKeyframe.title: Key a post-processing parameter
postAddKeyframe.description: Opens an animation channel on that parameter where it has none, and lays a key at the head. The value given is the one to SEE, and the delta against the stack is worked out here.

postRemoveKeyframe.title: Take a post-processing key off
postRemoveKeyframe.description: Removes the key standing at the head on that parameter. The channel stays, exactly as when a key is taken off from the band.

postSavePreset.title: Save the composition as a preset
postSavePreset.description: Keeps the stack in front under a name, on this machine. Nothing is written into the document or the project.

postRenamePreset.title: Rename a saved preset
postRenamePreset.description: Changes the name of a preset on this machine, named by its id or by the name it holds. What it contains does not move.

postDeleteSavedPreset.title: Forget a saved preset
postDeleteSavedPreset.description: Takes a saved preset off this machine. Compositions already applied do not change: a document holds its stack, never a reference.

componentAttach.title: Attach a component
componentAttach.description: Gives an object of the scene something to DO while the game runs — its health, its motion. This is how an object is made to move by itself: node.transform puts it somewhere once and it stays there. Refused when the object already carries one of that type.

componentDetach.title: Detach a component
componentDetach.description: Takes the component of the named type off an object of the scene. Refused when the object has not got one.

componentSetProperties.title: Set a component
componentSetProperties.description: Writes one field of a component the object carries. A field the component does not declare is ignored.

playStart.title: Start the game
playStart.description: Starts the game on the scene in front. Answers at once, so read the state with runtime.report.

playStop.title: Stop the game
playStop.description: Stops the game and puts the scene back as it was being edited.

playPause.title: Pause the game
playPause.description: Suspends the game without leaving it. Required before play.step.

playResume.title: Resume the game
playResume.description: Carries on from where the pause left the game, without catching up on the time it stood still.

playLoadScene.title: Send the game to another scene
playLoadScene.description: Loads another scene of the project into the running game, with an optional fade. The scene is named by its title or its id.

playStep.title: Step the game
playStep.description: Runs one or more fixed steps of a PAUSED game and answers its state. This is how a reading is taken without racing.

runtimeReport.title: Read the state of the game
runtimeReport.description: Answers the tick, the rate, the entity count, how many errors there are and the last lines the game wrote.

runtimeErrors.title: Read the faults of the game
runtimeErrors.description: Answers ADDRESSABLE faults — the script reference, the entity reference, the line and the column.

scriptList.title: List the scripts
scriptList.description: Answers every script of the project, with its reference and its length.

scriptRead.title: Read a script
scriptRead.description: Answers the text of a script, including what has not been saved yet.

scriptWrite.title: Write a script
scriptWrite.description: Writes a script into the project. Refused, with the line, when the file will not compile.

studioDescribe.title: Describe what is in front
studioDescribe.description: Answers the scene, an object, its components with their schema, its relations and what may still be added to it.

studioDocs.title: Read documented component or scripting settings
studioDocs.description: Answers the slice of documentation that answers one question — a component, or the surface a script sees.

studioBatch.title: Run a batch of calls
studioBatch.description: Runs a batch of calls as one, with a single question. Stops at the first refusal.

timelineAddSceneCue.title: Cue an event, media item or fade on the timeline
timelineAddSceneCue.description: Adds an event, a sound, a video or a transition to the timeline of the 3D SCENE. An event is a NAME put on the bus at the moment given, which a script hears through onMessage — that is how something is made to happen at a point of a cinematic, rather than by laying animation keys. A cinematic fade goes here, with list=transitions and what=fade. What the third field names depends on the list — an event name, an asset id, or a kind of transition. For a fade on a clip of an edit, that is clip.fade.

timelineRemoveSceneCue.title: Take a cue off the timeline
timelineRemoveSceneCue.description: Takes one cue off the timeline of the 3D SCENE — an event, a sound, a video or a transition, a cinematic fade among them. The id is read from the cues member of what scene.state answers, and nowhere else. To take a fade off a clip of an edit, that is clip.fade with a length of zero.

timelineSetPanelRows.title: Choose what the timeline offers
timelineSetPanelRows.description: Decides which rows the panel proposes. It never takes anything away from the engine, which plays the whole timeline regardless.

gameApplyTemplate.title: Lay out a game template
gameApplyTemplate.description: Lays the floor, the character and the objects of a kind of game into the open scene, and sets the camera and the gravity with them. One undo takes all of it back.

gameExport.title: Export the game
gameExport.description: Writes into a folder a game that runs in a browser with no studio, with the page, the runtime, the scenes, the transpiled scripts and only the assets they reach.

prefabDefine.title: Name a prefab
prefabDefine.description: Writes a scene of the project into game.json as a reusable piece, under the given name. With no document named, it is the scene in front.

prefabInstantiate.title: Instance a prefab
prefabInstantiate.description: Lays the objects of another scene document of the project into the open scene, with fresh ids, where it is asked for. A game already RUNNING is sent to another scene by play.loadScene, which this does not do.

memoryRecall.title: Recall what was learned
memoryRecall.description: Searches what the assistant NOTICED while working and answers the summaries it found, with their ids. What the person said the project is lives in the context cards.

memoryRead.title: Read one memory whole
memoryRead.description: Answers the DETAIL of one memory — what it refers to and where it came from — from an id memory.recall hands over. Recall gives the summaries; this is what « donne-moi le détail » asks for.

memoryWrite.title: Remember something about the project
memoryWrite.description: Writes down a working rule of this project, or something the assistant noticed while acting — how a thing is done here, what a file or an object is for. What the person says the project IS or AIMS AT is a context card instead. Replaces the one already standing on the same reference.

memoryForget.title: Forget a memory
memoryForget.description: Marks something the assistant noticed as forgotten. Nothing is erased from the file: what was learned stays traceable.

memoryLink.title: Link two memories
memoryLink.description: Adds a link from one memory to another, to say that one sheds light on the other.

consent.ask: Ask whoever you are acting for, then send this same call again, its consent parameter set to {{token}}. The token is single-use, lasts 5 minutes, and answers for this call alone.
consent.askInLot: Ask whoever you are acting for, then send this same batch again with a consent field set to {{token}} inside THIS call’s own input. The token is single-use, lasts 5 minutes, and answers for this call alone.

refusals.unknownCommand: No such command exists in the studio.
refusals.wrongSurface: No surface of the studio was there to take that command. Open the document or the panel it speaks to.
refusals.generatorClosed: The Generator was not open. It is now.
refusals.nothingPrepared: The Generator has no model armed at the moment.
refusals.notSubmitted: The generation did not go out.
refusals.badInput: The parameters given do not suit this action.
refusals.noProject: No project is open, and these paths are relative to one.
refusals.noConfirmer: That action needs a yes, and no window was there to give one.
refusals.noWindow: No studio window was in front to run that action.
refusals.timedOut: The request stood on screen unanswered, and was given up on.
refusals.noReference: The form carries no reference image to read a style from.
refusals.ambiguousLanding: Two destinations are possible and the studio would have asked, but a call from outside has no screen for the question. Name one: the wrong choice writes over an open file.
refusals.formChanged: The form changed after the cost was quoted. Nothing was sent — ask again for a fresh figure.
refusals.notFound: Nothing of that name is there to act on. The call itself was well formed.
refusals.notAllowed: The studio does not let a call from outside change that. Only its own window does.
refusals.nativeDialog: This command raises a system dialogue: the assistant can neither fill it in nor read it back. Use the action that takes a path.
refusals.notRenderable: The document in front has nothing this can render — an empty sky, a material with no channel, or an engine that is not mounted.
refusals.needsConsent: Nothing engaged: that call needs a consent token. The refusal carries a fresh one, and the same call sent back with it runs.
refusals.failed: The studio tried and it did not go through. The reason is in its activity journal, and it was not the parameters.
